card.title: Core utilities
card.blurb: The kernel every other package reaches for: type guards, grapheme-aware Unicode strings, a large text-validation toolbox, RFC 3339 date arithmetic on strings and epoch milliseconds, a GeoJSON-native spatial kernel with exact orientation predicates, and asm.js-style int32/float64 math.

card.title: Geospatial kernel
card.blurb: GeoJSON itself as the representation, not a geometry class: Shewchuk adaptive-precision orientation predicates, great-circle distance and area on the sphere, ring closure and winding, geohash, and a Hilbert-packed static R-tree behind the query engine's spatial joins.
card.perf: results asserted equivalent to the rivals before timing, and the point-in-polygon loss is published — an exact predicate costs

card.title: JSON addressing
card.blurb: The addressing and transformation standards as compilers: JSON Pointer, JSONPath, JSON Patch and Merge Patch, copy-on-write write operations, an XQuery-semantics query language written as JSON documents, JSLT stylesheets and the JTLT text front-end — one family, every grammar published as JSON Schema.

card.title: JSONPath
card.blurb: The complete RFC 9535 grammar as a compiler — every case of the official compliance corpus scored, normalized paths included.
card.perf: scored on the whole official compliance corpus

card.title: JSON Pointer
card.blurb: RFC 6901 with zero-allocation compiled getters, plus relative pointers — the $data hot path.
card.perf: compiled getters, far ahead of the npm package

card.title: JSON Patch
card.blurb: RFC 6902 and RFC 7396 as copy-on-write appliers: atomic, structure-sharing, and a change feed of written paths.
card.perf: measured against clone-and-interpret

card.title: JSON Query
card.blurb: XQuery 3.1 semantics — FLWOR, joins, grouping, quantifiers, folds and windows — as JSON documents with JSONPath leaves. Uncorrelated equijoins are planned as hash joins, and only where the rewrite is provably invisible.
card.perf: measured against fontoxpath and JSONata

card.title: JSLT
card.blurb: The stylesheet layer: JSONPath matches position, JSON Schema matches shape, query documents produce output. Identity transforms return the input reference. Operator packs register more — createJsltRegistry().use(mathPack)… adds $npv, $mean, $sqrt to JSLT, query and linq, and over @jarenjs/db the scalar subset pushes to SQLite as UDFs.
card.perf: proof-of-no-change without rebuilding the document; host operator packs are opt-in

card.title: JTLT
card.blurb: The text sibling of JSLT: template rules render JSON as Markdown, XML or source code — schema-matched rules turn one table document into SQLite or PostgreSQL DDL, and the xml method escapes interpolated data while literal markup passes raw.
card.perf: a front-end, not a second engine: compiles to JSLT

card.title: JSON Schema
card.blurb: Compiles schemas to specialized closures: annotation-driven unevaluated* with statically-elided checks, dynamic refs, $data, the $query cross-field keyword and structured, localizable errors.
card.perf: scored on the official suite per draft; the Ajv ratio is measured, not claimed

card.title: Format validators
card.blurb: One canonical name → predicate registry for the string, numeric, date-time, addressing and geospatial formats, shared by the validator and the form model so the two can never drift.

card.title: Draft meta-schemas
card.blurb: The bundled JSON Schema draft meta-schemas and their vocabularies, so draft detection, $vocabulary processing and meta-validation answer offline — a validator that never fetches a schema from the network to find out which draft it is reading.

card.title: Schemas as TypeScript
card.blurb: Build-time artifacts from JSON documents: a schema graph flattened into a published type model and rendered by a JTLT stylesheet per target — TypeScript declarations, Markdown reference docs — with a check mode that fails CI when a schema moved and the types did not.

card.title: Contract
card.blurb: One document declares your JSON-in/JSON-out operations — kind, policy, HTTP binding — and compiles once into validators, transport normalizers and a static-beats-variable path matcher. The same contract serves over HTTP, in-process through the local binding, and across a MessagePort or a worker, binds into an @jarenjs/app document as generated task slots, and projects to OpenAPI 3.1, TypeScript, Markdown and AI tool definitions from the one source.
card.perf: measured against a hand-composed router doing the same work — the dispatch loss published beside the wins

card.title: Forms
card.blurb: JSON Schema to a framework-agnostic field tree with three validation layers on one stack — per keystroke, cross-field, and authoritative on submit.
card.perf: this site renders forms with it

card.title: Locale packs
card.blurb: Message catalogs for the validator's and the form model's errors plus the calendar language the date kernel refuses to invent, one pack per language, over the stable msgids and raw params every error carries — so switching language re-renders the text and re-validates nothing.

card.title: View
card.blurb: UIs as JSON: the tagged-array vnode format, a keyed DOM patcher that skips unchanged subtrees in O(1), an SSR serializer and a registered-widget escape hatch for irreducibly imperative islands. The grammar ships as JSON Schema, so a constrained decoder cannot emit a structurally invalid interface — and an opt-in safe-render profile sanitizes an untrusted one. Running a view as data costs engine time against a hand-written build, and the benchmark publishes that price beside the win.
card.perf: hand-written vnodes outbuild the mainstream frameworks; the stylesheet pays for views-as-data — both published

card.perf: measured against marked, markdown-it and micromark; constant-time re-render

card.title: Charts
card.blurb: Headless SVG charts from JSON/JSONX/JOSL definitions: geometry-free ASTs, thirteen chart types from pie to GeoJSON maps, schema-validated, and a stream adapter that builds charts live from the incremental readers — replay a document chunk by chunk, or go live on real market data.
card.perf: incremental ticks that stay flat as the series grows

card.title: Studio
card.blurb: The project IDE: a multi-file project — an app document beside the schema, view, actions, model and query files it sits with — is one document, each file validated against its own published grammar, assembled into runnable artifacts and hosted live by the studio widget. The engine is headless; the component layer is the IDE.

card.title: Play
card.blurb: The engine playground: pick a JSON engine — JSON Schema, JSONPath, JSON Pointer, JSON Patch, query, JSLT, JTLT, JOSL, CSV, Markdown, Mermaid, Contract — feed it an input and one or more datasets from a curated example library, and watch it run. Understand an engine standalone before composing it in the Studio. The engine is headless; the component is the playground UI.

card.title: JOSL, JSONX & CSV
card.blurb: TOML 1.0 as a superset with JavaScript's obvious values first-class, the same extensions over JSON as JSONX, and a self-healing CSV reader — each with an incremental streaming reader whose chunks may split any token, all reporting one unified event with pointer-able paths.

card.title: JOSL
card.blurb: A strict TOML 1.0 superset with JavaScript-obvious values and streaming document-order events. The only engine in our benchmark passing the full toml-test suite — and the same reader family streams JSONX, strict JSON and CSV. Opt into detach and a record is handed over and forgotten, so a document larger than memory reads in a flat 0.1 MB.
card.perf: scored on the whole toml-test corpus

card.title: CSV
card.blurb: RFC 4180 strict by default, and self-healing on demand: an unclosed quote, a stray quote inside a value or a ragged row is read the way that loses the least — and every fix is reported with a code, a line and a column, where other parsers heal silently or reject the file. Wholesale and chunk-streaming share one grammar path.
card.perf: reports what it repaired, instead of guessing quietly

card.title: AI assistant
card.blurb: Browser-side AI with bring-your-own-key: one OpenAI-compatible client (OpenRouter / Ollama / LM Studio), an incremental SSE decoder, retry with Retry-After, structured output with local-validation repair, token-budget compaction, a bounded agent loop and WebMCP registration.
card.perf: tool calls validated by Jaren before they run

card.title: Flow — executable workflows
card.blurb: Executable workflows as JSON: pure state machines and statecharts, concurrent dataflow, and composed workflows with durable wait/resume. Guards are query documents and effects come back as data. The Flow studio edits, runs and animates flat machines and DAGs live.
card.perf: a machine survives a JSON round trip with its guards; XState’s functions do not

card.title: LINQ — the suite, by code
card.blurb: One package writes every document the suite runs: C#-familiar chains whose output is a plain query document, and eight pens that write the others the same way — a JSON Schema, a database model, a JSLT stylesheet, a migration with its transform typed old row to new row, a contract, a state machine and a dataflow, an application, a form. A recording proxy captures the callback, the emitter folds stages into one FLWOR document, and the same chain runs in memory, over streams (one bounded mapAsync boundary), or pushed whole to a store's entity sets through the provider seam — or through the typed client that fronts the store under `./db`, over one declared edge.
card.perf: one operator set, byte-identical documents through the sync and async drivers

card.title: Data — documents in SQLite
card.blurb: Documents AND entities in SQLite behind driver and dialect seams: a pushdown planner that renders guarded parameter-bound SQL, one-statement graph loads, a copy-on-write unit of work with optimistic concurrency, generated entity types, and a jaren-db CLI whose migrations rebuild tables the documented twelve-step way.
card.perf: the two-level graph load runs in ONE statement; statement counts published beside every timing
